Educational Insights Design & Drill All Aboard Train, 30 Piece Take Apart Toy with Electric Drill Toy, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 3+ [[VIDEOID:979dc2c95d283020e887dc97f4539982]] There is supposed to be a motorized drill included with this set, but only the drill socket was included. Happily, the conductor has a hole on the bottom that can be used to tighten or loosen the bolts. My three-year-old niece was content with using this as is and loves the train so much as a toy that I'll give it 3 stars, but I think many children would prefer the fun of the motorized drill. When you press a button, the train makes a chu-chu sound and a very dim white light comes out the front. You can't see the light unless you're looking for it. The "design and drill" is basically some bolts to screw on to hold the covers and the wheels in place. There were several colors of bolts you can choose from to make different "designs."

The engine measures 10 inches long by 6 inches wide by 6 inches tall. The wagon measures 7.5 inches long by 6 inches wide by 3.75 inches tall. The wagon bed is 2 inches deep. The caboose measures 7.5 inches long 6 inches wide and 5 inches tall. Three AAA batteries are needed to power the drill according to the instruction manual, and two AAA batteries are needed for the train engine for the sound and light. The wheels roll smoothly and securely, and it is easy to connect the three sections of the train together, so it is a good toy not just a building activity. There are some extra bolts in case some are lost. The train is sturdy and can withstand the rough treatment of a 3-year-old armed with a plastic hammer.

RRIBOUDWAN Maze Magnetic Puzzle Game for Kids Ages 4-8, Brain Teasers Puzzle Game for Children, Educational Learning Toy, Think Fun Toy, Logic Game Important: you must place the card on top of the box for the magnetic pieces to stick. Nowhere in the instructions does it mention this. Oddly, the magnets are separate and not pre-attached to the pieces. Of course, you can place the card on any flat surface, but the magnets will not stick unless you place it on top of the lid.

This comes in a very nice, heavy cardboard box as shown in the pictures. The box measures 9.5” x 8” x 2.5”. You have to work a little bit to get the lid off. The box is actually about twice the thickness that it needs to be. Nonetheless, you can store other things in it if you wish.

There are 30 sheets/levels to complete. But you’re doing the exact same thing on all of them. Meaning that you are connecting the water inlet from one side to the other so the crocodile can take a shower. All of the cards are numbered in the lower right corner. Each card is a little more challenging than the last. But, to be honest, after doing a few of these, some kids may find it boring. It would’ve been nice if the cards had more variety. Meaning different subjects and such, even if the actual tasks were virtually the same.

Personally, I think this is more of a “one and done” sort of item. I highly doubt kids are going to want to do this again and again. Works better for a classroom setting. So multiple children will be able to use it.

This set is made in China and being sold by Chinese company on Amazon.

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels 20-Pack of 1:64 Scale Toy Sports & Race Cars, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary) It might seem as if 20 cars is too much at once. Nope! It is wonderful.

Days as a five year-old were best filled with playing in complete abandon. The freedom proffered by youth needed only a few toys to complete the ever-present joy. A few toys which mattered included several tattered but friendly books, a truck or two, an odd shovel and bucket, and, the coup de grace, a Hot Wheels car. Mattel makes a track as well, but a well-made car could take a boy places. This set of 20 is what kindergartners drool over.

A boy has everything in this set: vehicles of all colors, a few truck varieties, some funny looking cars. There are plenty, and frankly, since a few will invariably wind up lost under the couch, eaten by the dog, and buried with other treasures in the garden, having 20 quickly becomes justified.

Why a Hot Wheels car? Because they are made with hard steel. They are painted with a slick color. They hold up to frequent tastings, sand grindings, dirt smearings and other nonsense that comes with power racing in a sandbox. Sticky chocolate wipes off with warm water, and grime comes out with a good spray under the faucet.

The wheels themselves have a bounce peculiar to a genuine Hot Wheels vehicle. That's how my brother and I made sure it had adequate fuel. Ten bounces should be enough, we figured, and usually, we were right.

I fully recommend the "Hot Wheels 20-Car Gift Pack."

Anthony Trendl
AmericanSpeechwriter.com
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels 20-Pack of 1:64 Scale Toy Sports & Race Cars, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary)

Chillafish BOX: Connectable Toy Storage and Play System, Blue/Red Love:
- The look.
- The stackability options.
- The strength of the outer cube (Brick).

Dislike:
- The storage bin section feels like it's a much weaker plastic than the rest - so much so that mine arrived with visible scratches and what looks to be either a flaw in the plastic or like someone pushed on it enough to not break it but start to weaken it.
- The cost ($49.99 at the time of this review) plus an additional $14.99 if you want the matching table top.

Neutral:
- The safety strap is rather difficult to attach to the cube because it is basically a really tight fit and has to push up inside the bottom slot and out through the upper slot. Not impossible but it'll take a few minutes.
- The size. Most storage cubes we have are a little bigger.

Optional:
- The table top is and additional / optional purchase. Because of the way the bricks are designed, the top does sit perfectly on top of the cube. There is nothing holding it in place, so it's probably not safe around young just starting to stand and grab onto things. It's easy to pull off.

Overall:
If these were just a little bigger or cheaper or both, we'd probably buy a bunch of them. As it is, I'll just have the one as a novelty near / on my desk. If you don't mind the price, these are probably fine. For me, the size difference + cost of many other storage systems just isn't worth it.

I obviously cannot review how well the work with other cubes as I only have one. but I really don't see that adding enough value to make me leave my more plain storage tubs.
text_fidelity_b: Chillafish BOX: Connectable Toy Storage and Play System, Blue/Red

text_fidelity_a:
PLANET BAKE Donut Baking Kit - Vegan Chocolate Donuts with Pre-Measured Ingredients and No Added Sugar- Complete Chef Kit Idea for Boys and Girls ages 4-12 I'm not at all pleased with this donut kit. I like the idea -- a kit that includes everything needed to make baked, frosted donuts that kids (with supervision) can take on as a fun project. Unfortunately, the execution of the idea was not done well.

The items come in a flimsy cardboard box that is easily dented up in transit. It makes for a poor presentation should this be a gift item sent to child. Inside the box is a set of cheap silicone molds for the donuts, a packet of sprinkles and a sealed packet with the mixes. The sprinkle packet opened up in transit so there were sprinkles everywhere. Inside the sealed packet the frosting mix is in a pouch, but the donut mix is just loose in the pouch. Getting the frosting packet out was a very messy proposition.

Making the mix is simple (needs water and oil). The included silicone molds are very thin and flimsy, and need to be inserted into a muffin pan to minimize the chance of spilling. This is the step kids will need the most assistance with.

But even if the donuts bake properly, they are no treat to eat. The chocolate flavor is not pleasant, and is made even worse by the artificial sweetener aftertaste. The texture is not bad considering these are gluten-free, but the taste is not good to the point where these are barely (and I mean barely!) edible.

Two stars for the overall concept of a donut kit as a fun kid project (both making and decorating) but everything else is a fail.
text_fidelity_b: PLANET BAKE Donut Baking Kit - Vegan Chocolate Donuts with Pre-Measured Ingredients and No Added Sugar- Complete Chef Kit Idea for Boys and Girls ages 4-12

Ravensburger Neuschwanstein Castle 2000 Piece Panorama XXL Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults – Softclick Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly For the last 15 years my extended family has been assembling puzzles during our beach vacation at the North Carolina Outer Banks. We now have a well established family tradition of puzzling with increasingly challenging puzzles. For the last few years, only Ravensburgers will do. These puzzles are well made, with thick, solid cardboard with a bright, spill resistant color.

The difficult part about this puzzle are the vast blue and cloudy blue areas at the top, and the large amounts of snow covered tree limbs. At 132 cm wide, this puzzle is 4' 4" across, much wider than most coffee tables. We set up a specific rectangular folding table for puzzles like this, or push two together. I would judge this puzzle as on the "difficult" end for puzzles with 2,000 pieces (to be precise, it has 2,040 pieces!). It took our family a full week to work through all the branches, blues, snow, etc.

A nice thing about this puzzle is that even though its 2,000 pieces, the pieces are all a "large" nice size, which makes it more fun, and easier to tell one from another, and spot tiny differences in color and shape.

The insert in the box comes in a wide variety of languages, the pieces come inside the sturdy box wrapped in a bag. Its quality throughout.

Have fun!

text_fidelity_a:
Matchbox Aqua Cannon Fire Truck Rig [[VIDEOID:f267642283bcf2ef6b127013dc46be9b]] On the advertising, this says that it shoots 20 feet. I was really skeptical, and I was expecting it to only shoot 20 feet in the air. Now, I don't have a 20 foot ladder, so I can't tell for sure, but I'm pretty sure that this will shoot vertically 20 feet, and horizontally maybe even a little more.

The truck is big and bulky, which I really liked. And there are no small, removable parts, so it's probably good for kids of any age. It does shoot a pretty powerful stream of water, so the only danger is squirting friends, family, and pets in the eye.

Now, about the water, the truck doesn't hold very much water. It says that it will shoot 50 shots of water, and it does do that. This is a lot like one of those water conserving showers. It really doesn't use very much water, but you can't really tell that until you fill it up. So, it's not the best thing for a water fight. But it is a great gift for youngsters so they don't get their siblings too wet. And I did really like the bright, vivid colors.

The wheels rotate, but they can't turn. If you need to turn this, you'll need to pick it up and move it around. Really, the only movable part on this is the fire hose.

Pros:
+Big and bulky
+Fun for all ages
+Shoots water a long way
+You can position the fire hose a little

Cons:
-A little hard to aim
-Wheels can't turn right or left, only rotate straight ahead
-Doesn't hold a ton of water
-You can't build up pressure to do a power squirt
text_fidelity_b: Matchbox Aqua Cannon Fire Truck Rig

My first one had a small issue with the  power cord sometime cutting out.  I got my replacement and ZERO issues.  The programming of this does take a little study to understand and get it all figured out (the buttons presses can be redundant and and a mistake and you sometimes have to back out to the beginning).  Once you get the sequence down it is pretty easy to use.  It charges all my battery packs very well and at the set voltages and amperage. Readout is bright and easy to see even with my 53 yr old eyes.  The finish cycle beep is annoying but does get me to check and turn off the charger.  I have only been using it for 4.8 volt and 7.2 volt packs so far but there has been no heat issues.  Directions are so-so.  If your new to this type of charger there are some videos that are much better than the written directions.  If you have used any type of programmable charge then this will be easy enough to figure out and use from just the written direction.  Love the auto battery test and the reverse polarity warning.  Makes this a much safer option.  The fireproof bag is large enough for most packs and Hopefully will never have to be tested.  I don't generally need to charge my batteries while away from an outlet but it is nice to know that this can handle that also.  Just very pleased with the entire package.

You can see how there are pieces of this product that come lodged incorrectly including the skull which does not stay in its designated hole. The large intestine looks like it's already been pulled apart by a child passed its point of stretch as it is extremely thin at the connection area.

Also--I if I as a teacher could not even put this item in full back together, I can only imagine how difficult this would be for a child of any age to maneuver as well.

If this company would just give more effort into putting out a quality product it would be extremely useful across-the-board and save them so much money in returns if they would just take the small effort to fix these ongoing issues that so many purchasers report.

I was able to get a 25% refund on my initial purchase with being able to keep the item as I explained I do not want to do a third replacement bit instead that I would rather just find a innovative way to make the issues I've experienced usable for teaching my students.

If you get this product don't settle for a poor quality item...they used to be made so well and now this company has made cheaply made pieces of it the regular. Stick to your guns on insisting on either a working product and/or a refund.

Wish you all the best with this item.

text_fidelity_a: Cephalofair Games: Gloomhaven, Award-Winning Strategy Board Game, For 1 to 4 Players, 60 to 120 Minute Play Time, For Ages 14 and up Me and my brothers have been buying board games for a while now. But no other board game takes as much dedication to play, store, and maintain, as this one. Aside from maybe pen and paper D&D. You get a box around the size of a family dog crammed with game. There's a reason there are YouTube videos dedicated to various ways to store this game's pieces. LMAO Along with various storage solutions sold on the internet. It's a beast to store. A beast to set up. But for all the work you put up with, is the actual game worth the hefty price tag? Hell yes. The ongoing campaign really gives you a sense of accomplishment as you trudge through one dungeon after another in your pursuit to fill your map with markers. Oh, and that map. We hung ours in a frame and laminated the countless stickers and markers so that they could be stuck to the frame glass with mounting strips. We proudly hang it on the wall showing everything we've done. Our band of mercenaries, Duke's Coinpurse, have opened up a LOT of content with hours and hours of gameplay. And we're not done with it by a long shot. Not even counting the expansion we bought for it. Now there are a few things that are kind of annoying. Like some of the personal quests that you may get that will want to complete content you already completed, or character classes you've already unlocked. Making your character's personal quest pointless or do some back tracking to complete. So there is kind of a miss-step in the order of reveals for some things. Your group is going to argue about rules in the rulebook. I can almost guarantee it. LOL Not that the rules are hard to understand, but there are so many that you're going to be dragging it out to double check something if you're anything like my group. LOL But it's about as close to an actual D&D campaign as you can get. The character classes you play aren't all that fleshed out aside from a backstory on the back of their card, and the game has city events and road events that play out with a scenario that the group chooses from a multiple choice outcome. But the immersion is a little lacking in that you don't actually "role play" per say as you do just dungeon crawl. But it's still a Hell of a lot of fun. Just prepare to work for that fun. Because it's a huge, long game. Scoundrel4Life
text_fidelity_b: Cephalofair Games: Gloomhaven, Award-Winning Strategy Board Game, For 1 to 4 Players, 60 to 120 Minute Play Time, For Ages 14 and up

You get a nice looking cigar box, a bunch of poker chips and a surprisingly light little rule book that packs a lot of fiddly into a very small package (You can do this, or if you do that, you can do between one and three types of thingy, unless you've already taken the what'sit and then refer to page three).

Overall, a very fun and short game if:
1. You have a well-chosen and probably an experienced player be the don. There is actually quite a lot to this role, and a lot of consultation with that fiddly little rule about what you can initially take. The rest of the game is super simple, but first time players will want to see a round first. The person playing as the don has to basically command the entire game, so choosing a shy or confused player can completely ruin the experience.
2. You like the Resistance and games similar, but want something just a little different. This will provide that.
3. You have a group large enough to play this 6 - 12 player game. It handles double digits quite well.
text_fidelity_b: Mafia de Cuba

text_fidelity_a:
Dixit Board Game 2021 Refresh | Storytelling Game for Kids and Adults | Fun Family Party Game | Creative Kids Game | Ages 8+ | 3-8 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Libellud This is a completely different kind of game and the idea of stars and lanterns is abstract. It says it is easy to learn, but to be honest, don't bring your friends together to learn the game. You should set it up, read through the directions and pretend to have two friends with you to understand what is going on. THEN you can explain the game to your friends. The reason is because you can tell this game was not designed in America, there are a few minor English mistakes. The directions have interesting choice of words. So I'm going to try my best by using parentheses to show the words they used in the directions.

The goal of the game is when a word card is revealed, you try to figure out which dixit (picture) cards match that word--by the picture itself, the color(s), inspiration, characters, etc. Then you mark an X (cross) for each dixit card you feel matches that word. At the same time, you want to choose cards you think your friends will choose. If your friends chose that card too, both of you earn stars (sparks) and so on. If they didn't, then you lose (fall) and stop there. If you marked X for too many dixit cards (hoping to get a lot of points), more likely your friends won't have that same card marked and that will make you lose. You have to work like a team, trying to figure out what your friends will choose and win. (This is what they mean by the word, greedy.) This is a good way to teach kids how to perceive the pictures and THINK of others and what they could be thinking, again a "teamwork." This is where it is supposed to be fun. My daughter liked it, but my son didn't like it.

I have one suggestion for you as parents or caregiver of a child age 8 or over. (Ages for the game is for 8+.) I suggest you form the first few turns, you handpick the words you feel your child will be able to "match" then go from there. You handpicking and seeing a few cards in advance honestly does not change the game. The game actually entirely relies on the other players' dixit card choices.

There is one rule that seems pointless. Of course you need to read the directions first to understand what I"m talking about. Here I go anyway--suppose you "fall" then at the end of the game when everyone is ready to score. If you have some sparks and a super-spark from one of your dixit cards that you marked off (crosses), you wipe away one star (but not the super-spark star) then count the remaining stars (sparks). The super-spark star has the same point value as the other sparks so I'm not sure why it makes a difference to wipe off a star or a super-spark star.

This game is Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. It's also created in China and I don't know that it's going to be that great, at least for some U.S. audiences.
text_fidelity_b: Dixit Board Game 2021 Refresh | Storytelling Game for Kids and Adults | Fun Family Party Game | Creative Kids Game | Ages 8+ | 3-8 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Libellud

Just My Style Name Bracelet Maker by Horizon Group USA The loom is intended to make it easier to make braid or bead bracelets. The 6 spools come pre-wrapped with different types of cording. I didn't particularly care for their pre-wrapped selection, however, the spools can be wrapped with whatever cord or thread you want to use. Then you pop the spools into the dispenser section of the loom and slide the axle into place. We had some trouble getting the axle out again. The spools stay in place just fine without the axle, so we have no plans to use it again. You measure out 8 to 12 inches of cord for each strand to create a braided bracelet. You slip the cord into the foam slots near the spools to hold the cord in place, then braid using your own design or the instruction booklet directions. The booklet describes how to make a 3 strand braid, 6 strand braid, braided bracelet where one strand is first beaded, and a friendship bracelet. Though well-illustrated, the instructions were not always clear.

For beaded bracelets, you remove the green foam insets, choose a beading pattern, and set up the beads on the tray. The tray does make threading the beads easier. You place cords on either side of the beads on the board and use the included needle and thread to string the beads and attach them to the cords in rows. Except for the axle, everything worked fine. It would have been nice if the beads were packaged in sealed in zip bags or the like as they keep spilling. I ended up finding bags to put them in.
text_fidelity_b: Just My Style Name Bracelet Maker by Horizon Group USA

Magformers Hi-Tech LED Lighted Set (55-pieces) I was sort of surprised at how much this light set cost. I probably wouldn't have bought it due to that fact. However, if you have the bucks I think your kids will be very pleased with it. I have two kids ages 10 and almost 12. I got the Magformer Light set in the mail yesterday afternoon and they have been playing almost non-stop with it. It's not unusual for my kids to play with something for a few hours then never touch it again. However, this is the second day and they are still going strong with this set.

It does stimulate the imagination and the pieces are pretty cool imho. They adhere fairly strongly to each other by using internal magnets. They come in various shapes and cool colors and have a battery pack that can be attached to cause the entire creation to light up in multiple colors. The husband and I both had to wear helmets that emitted wonderful colors.....sorry no pics (thank gawd). A USB cable comes with the set to be used to recharge the battery pack.

The kids have multiple Zhu Zhu pets and have been having a blast with those silly things and light set at the same time by building lighted carry cages, homes, space ships and everything else you can think of and cram a zhu-zhu pet inside of. I like this light set a lot, it gives the kids something different and obviously very fun to do, and it has kept their attention now for 2 days straight. I asked them how much they liked it and they both hollered, "We LOVE it!".
text_fidelity_b: Magformers Hi-Tech LED Lighted Set (55-pieces)

The set of river rocks included is great, with varied sizes and shapes.  All super smooth and great painting surfaces.  The paint containers are all connected and the lids are VERY difficult to get open without spilling paint from the force needed to pry the plastic apart.  The colors are rich and bold though. I'll say this though, the paints take FOREVER to dry down to the point that they can be handled safely.  It took three solid days for the thin layers of paints to dry without coming off on our hands.

text_fidelity_a:
ThinkFun Zingo Sight Words Award Winning Early Reading Game for Pre-K to 2nd Grade - Toy of the Year Finalist, A Fun and Educational Game Developed by Educators for Boys and Girls, Multicolor My boys are 3, 5, and 7(almost 8), and they all enjoy this game. As a bonus, it requires NO batteries!

Both the game boards and the game pieces have both pictures and words on them. Your child doesn't have to be able to read to play the game, but it does make the picture/word connection, to an extent. The game goes so fast that even I tend to mostly just look at the picture, and ignore the words. There is still a slight connection, though, and every little bit helps when a little one is learning words.

The game comes with 7 game boards. These are double sided. The green side is for a less competitive game, and better for the littlest ones. There aren't that many shared pictures on this side, and the players aren't in so much of a rush to grab the tiles. The red side has a bit more competition, since there are more pictures in common. The players have to rush to grab a matching tile, before someone else grabs it.

Each game goes really quick, so you're not spending a ton of time on each game. There are a few different options for playing the game. You can go the traditional "Bingo" route, or you can match designs, play multiple cards, or even fill up the whole card, which is what my oldest prefers. The traditional route is just way too quick for my children's tastes.

Their favorite part of the game is the Zinger. It's super easy to load the tiles, and then slide them into view. They have to take turns sliding the tiles into view, because it's so much fun. The only negative we've seen is the fact that sometimes it seems the same tile is being played over and over(in a row). When you first open the box, you'll have to mix these tiles up, since they are placed together matched. If you don't mix them up, you WILL have the same tile continue to show up in a row. Even then, it sometimes happens that the same one will keep showing up. It is easy to dump them out, mix them up, and then reload them, though.

This is a super simple game, but so much fun for little ones! I even enjoy playing it with them, which is pretty important.
text_fidelity_b: ThinkFun Zingo Sight Words Award Winning Early Reading Game for Pre-K to 2nd Grade - Toy of the Year Finalist, A Fun and Educational Game Developed by Educators for Boys and Girls, Multicolor

Creativity for Kids Sensory Bin: Dinosaur Dig - Dinosaur Toys for Toddler Boys and Girls My child really likes this sensory bin. It’s a perfect indoor activity that has an outdoor activity feel (sand box and water table vibes). The sand is dense and forms well (kinetic play sand), and the water beads definitely give it a beach vibe. I added the small square bin inside to contain the water beads. I did not activate all of the water beads at once, that way we can make some fresh ones whenever we need to (they take about 3 hours to reach full size soaking in water).

One con is that the rim at the top of the bin itself is rough and very slim, and it leaves marks on our arms when we’ve played with it for a bit of time, which ends up being somewhat uncomfortable. A wider and more rounded rim on the bin would greatly improve the comfort while playing.

Another con is that the sand doesn’t sift very well with the yellow scooper. It’s perfect for shoveling the sand around, but not for sifting this denser type of play sand.

Despite some minor dislikes, the entire set is very entertaining for my preschooler, and it keeps us entertained as a fun winter activity.

text_fidelity_a: NATURALIFE 1byone Professional Bubble Machine with High Output, Automatic Blowing Mechanism for Outdoor or Indoor Use Started to buy one of the more expensive models but noticed this one didn't have any mention of foaming issues so decided for the price to give it a try. WOW! This thing is great! Thousands of bubbles most just under tennis ball size but some smaller. If you use the Gazillion Bubble solution you get beautiful iridescent bubbles that drift a long way before breaking. It works best and the bubble sdrift farther if you can get it up off the ground. A breeze helps too. I set it on the top step of a 3-step ladder and that was perfect. This machine is a bubble solution hog but it couldn't be any less and produce this volume of bubbles. Seems to run maybe 20 minutes or so on a fill and you get about 4 fills from a bottle of the 2 liter Gazillion Bubbles solution. It can make a but of a mess on the ground under the machine so be sure to place it somewhere that doesn't matter or is easy to clean. I didn't find the machine all that difficult to clean after using but you have to have a little patience. Hold it upside down and use the garden hose on low flow to wash out the solution tray being careful not to wet the motor or switch.. We ran this off and on over the 3 day July 4th weekend and it ran perfectly. Kids and adults both were amazed. If you want a bubble machine and don't want to spend a lot of money get this one.

text_fidelity_a:
Repos JUST01 Just One, Various There are a lot of "just one word clues" games out there, from Codenames and Decrypto to games like Funglish, Crosstalk or Word Slam, and this game is yet another to add to that group. I think, however, that it's my secnd favorite of the bunch, and if you need a Codenames Killer, this might be up your alley.

In this team game, one player is attempting to guess a word that the rest of their team knows. Each team member writes down one word only, then compares to see if any matches are detected. If they are, those cards are discarded, and the guesser is left with fewer clues. Therefore, the more obtuse clues you get, the more you'll have, but it can be more difficult to deduce the word than if you're given a few obvious clues.

What I like about this game is that it manages to be a louder than usual team game with secrets. In Codenames or Crosstalk, two previous iterations of the concept, games are fun, but often it's players staring at the board in silence. In this one, you still can't say much, but it does lend itself to quicker play, and it's easier to communicate more freely once you have your clues written since your work is done, and the stress of the round is over for the clue-givers. This is a hard game, and it's definitely a word game, but lends itself to being an excellent family gathering game.
text_fidelity_b: Repos JUST01 Just One, Various

text_fidelity_a:
Nasco WA04313 Human Body Fat Replica, 5 lb. Most reviews mention the mind-boggling size of the model; I figured that it was because when we gain fatty tissue, it's distributed in a thin layer over our bodies, so seeing it as a lump would be surprising to most people.

     Even with the warnings, I was still shocked! It looked like it had to be 8-10 pounds, not a mere 5! And it FELT like 6-8 pounds...

After a while, I got curious as to why it seemed so disproportionately large. I'm aware that I consistently make terrible (truly awful) estimations of volumes, distances, and weights, so I measured it, just to get the actual numbers.

     My kitchen scale gave the model's mass as 5.293 pounds. That's a forgivable degree of error: 6%. Definitely closer than my awful guesstimate of 6-8 pounds.

     I used displacement to measure the volume as 11.75 cups. [I filled a container to overflowing with water. I added the model to displace some water, then removed the model. I carefully measured how much water I added to completely refill the container.]

     Google conversions gives 11.75 cups as being 169.6 in^3. Various sites list the volume of a pound of adipose tissue as being 29 in^3, 29.5 in^3, 30.08 in^3, and 30.42 in^3.

Using the model's volume and the lowest density, I calculate the model's representative mass as:
169.6 in^3 ÷ 30.42 in^3/lbs = 5.577 lbs

And using the highest density to calculate my model's "mass":
169.6 in^3 ÷ 29 in^3/lbs = 5.8 lbs (17% greater than 5 pounds, but well under my 8-10 pound guess.)

So whether you are measuring by weight or volume, the model is 6-17% oversized. That's far more accurate than seemed possible.

Obviously the manufacturer had to compromise between approximating the coloration, texture, pliablity, volume, and weight. I'm not a surgeon, so I'm clueless as to the accuracy of the coloration, texture, and pliablity. I am disappointed that the volume (which was the characteristic I was most interested in) was off by more than 5%.
text_fidelity_b: Nasco WA04313 Human Body Fat Replica, 5 lb.

Kids as little as 3 love hiding and seeking and older adults love the memories of hiding and seeking out your playmates from their youth. The game can be played with 2 to 7 players.

This game is beautifully made with hard cardboard of a nice dark looking forest with a stone path. While putting the trees, stump and rock formations together, you will want to put the die under a light so it will glow in the dark for game play. You then place the masks on the Shadowling creatures. The Seeker gets to roll the die and move the lantern, after his eyes are closed, so the other player (s) can hide the little masked Shadowlings.

As the Seeker moves around the board, should any light hit any Shadowling- exposing them, their mask is removed and they are frozen and cannot move until another Shadowling can come and help him. Should all the Shadowlings end up together hiding in the same spot with their masks on, they win. Should the Seeker expose them all, freezing them, the Seeker wins.
